tasks.short: Answer telephones at the front desk, route calls, write messages for residents and staff, and deliver messages.

steps.what: Residential advisor answers telephones and routes calls
Residential advisor writes messages for residents and staff on paper slips
Residential advisor delivers messages to residents' rooms and staff

tasks.design: A short call menu on the residence phone line ({TELEPHONY}) sends maintenance calls to the facilities desk and plays opening hours, so the advisor takes fewer routine calls. Messages are typed into the residence system ({OTHER}), which notifies the resident or staff member on their phone; the advisor walks only urgent messages and parcels. Talking with callers who need a person stays with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every call came to the desk and messages were paper slips walked to rooms.
tasks.enabler_now: Phone menus and residence apps with notifications are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Parents in a panic need a person at once.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing that a caller is worried about a resident's safety.

evidence.claim: Phone menus can route calls by choice; residence apps can notify residents of messages.

assumptions: Boundary: from the incoming call to the message delivered; repairs are outside.
Input contract: residents' phone numbers in the residence system; fallback is paper slips.
Callers pick a menu option in a few seconds; a little caller time is priced.
Urgent calls still reach the advisor.
research_questions: Do routine calls to the desk fall?

incremental.description: Residential advisor keeps the call menu and opening hours current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly urgent calls; high: many routine calls and messages.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with students about family, financial and educational problems, look up where to refer them, refer them with consent, and note the talk briefly.

steps.what: Residential advisor counsels students in handling family, financial and educational problems
Residential advisor looks up where to refer the student
Residential advisor refers the student to student services by e-mail
Residential advisor notes the talk briefly

tasks.design: A referral overview of the university's student services, financial aid and local help ({DOCS}) shows who handles what and how to reach them, so the advisor does not search. Referrals go on a short form with the student's consent that lands at the right service. Counselling the student stays with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Referral addresses were searched each time and referrals sent by e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Referral overviews and consent forms are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Students in crisis need a warm handover, not a form.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a proud student to accept help with money.

reach.learn: Whether referrals arrive with consent and context.

evidence.claim: Referral overviews and consent forms can route students to the right service.
Notes on students' health or family problems may be special category data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student concern to the talk noted; counselling by professionals is outside.
Input contract: overview kept by student services; fallback is searching and e-mail.
Students give consent in about the time the e-mail took.
research_questions: Do referred students reach the service more often?

incremental.description: Residential advisor reports outdated entries in the overview.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few referrals; high: many students needing referral.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan unit meetings and invite residents, hold the meeting, write notes and agreements, share them with residents, and follow up agreements.

steps.what: Residential advisor plans unit meetings and invites residents with posters
Residential advisor holds regular meetings with each assigned unit
Residential advisor writes notes and agreements
Residential advisor pins the notes on the unit board
Residential advisor follows up agreements with residents

tasks.design: Unit meetings recur in the residence app ({CHAT}) with an invitation and reminder to every resident of the unit, replacing posters. Notes use a short template, and once written they are posted to the unit's channel in the app. Holding the meeting and following up stay with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Meetings were announced with posters and notes pinned on a board.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence apps send invitations and posts to unit members.
tasks.still_hard: Residents skip meetings whatever the invitation.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a dispute about the shared kitchen before it grows.

evidence.claim: Residence apps can send invitations, reminders and posts to unit members.

assumptions: Boundary: from the unit list to agreements followed up; house rules are outside.
Input contract: unit membership in the residence system; fallback is posters and boards.
Residents read the app as they read the board; no added resident time.

incremental.description: Residential advisor updates unit membership after moves.

approvals.approved_version: The notes as written by the advisor in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few units; high: many units with monthly meetings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect residents' daily activity logs, count supplies used, tally the figures, write the required report, check it, and send it to the housing office.

steps.what: Residential advisor compiles information on residents' daily activities from staff logs
Residential advisor counts the quantities of supplies used
Residential advisor tallies the figures in a spreadsheet
Residential advisor prepares the required report
Residential advisor e-mails the report to the housing office

tasks.design: Staff log activities in the residence system ({OTHER}) instead of sending notes, and supplies are booked out by scanning shelf labels, so a report view ({BI}) tallies activities and supplies used per period. The required report is a template filled from that view; the advisor adds comments and checks it, and once checked it goes to the housing office. Counting supplies at period end stays with the advisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Logs came by e-mail and figures were tallied by hand in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Residence systems log activities; report views tally them.
tasks.still_hard: Staff forget to scan supplies they take.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining in the report why one unit needs more support.
tasks.altitude: The advisor checks figures instead of tallying them.

evidence.claim: Residence systems can log activities and tally them in report views.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff logs to the report sent; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: staff log in the residence system; supplies labelled; fallback is e-mail and spreadsheets.
Checking the report stays with the advisor.
Staff log in the system in about the time an e-mail took.

incremental.description: Residential advisor corrects missed supply scans.

approvals.approved_version: The report as checked by the advisor in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few activities and supplies; high: a large residence with weekly reports.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The residential advisor keeps talking with callers and students, holding unit meetings and checking reports; paper slips, posters and hand tallies shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An advisor with more time for residents.
